thread:
maya (PM): quick sync — need a decision on ordering for Optimize toolkit: quantization, batching, caching. we have multiple customer asks and limited eng cycles. thoughts?
anjali (Eng-ML): +1 to decide fast. my quick gut: batching -> quantization -> caching for infrastructure ROI, but depends on workloads.
ryan (Eng-runtime): interesting. batching gives big throughput wins but is infra-surface area heavy (scheduling, queuing, fair-share). if we push batching first we need robust backpressure.
chris (CSE): customers in fin+health want deterministic latencies and lower token cost. several asked for prefix caching specifically (repeated system prompts). caching would unblock some enterprise renewals.
maya (PM): ok tradeoffs. let's try RICE-ish quick sketch? impact/effort/confidence.
anjali (Eng-ML): here's a tiny table (very rough):
```
Feature      Impact (1-10)  Effort (1-10)  Confidence
Batching         8              7             0.7
Quantization     6              4             0.8
Caching          7              5             0.6
```
score = (impact * confidence) / effort -> batching ~0.8, quant ~1.2, caching ~0.84
ryan (Eng-runtime): numbers make quant sound best, but they ignore infra risk. quant has high safety/compatibility work for accuracy regressions. if we land quant first we should bake eval gating.
chris (CSE): prioritize by revenue risk: customers threatening to delay contracts want caching now. caching could be scoped to customer-specific KV prefix cache initially. low-risk rollout.
maya (PM): two paths: revenue-driven (caching first for renewals) or technical-leverage (quant first for low-hanging cost wins). we should pick one and define launch criteria.
anjali (Eng-ML): launch criteria proposals:
- Quantization: end-to-end eval regressions <= 1% across critical eval set, model-specific profiles, rollout canary to 5% traffic, automatic rollback on quality drop.
- Batching: sustained p95 token latency within SLA for mixed workload, graceful degradation under overload, visible per-route metrics.
- Caching: hit rate >= 15% for targeted routes, no P99 regressions, ACLs for private caches (enterprise requirement).
ryan (Eng-runtime): sequencing option C: light-weight caching for targeted routes (edge cache for prefixes) -> quick wins for CS -> spend remaining sprint on quantization infra prototypes -> larger batching in next quarter. gives customer wins and buys time for batching design.
maya (PM): that seems pragmatic. what's the estimated eng effort if we do small-scope caching first?
ryan (Eng-runtime): 2 sprints (2 engs) for an MVP: per-customer config, simple LRU prefix cache, metrics + feature flag. then 3-4 sprints for hardened global cache.
anjali (Eng-ML): quant prototype: 3 sprints for per-model quant profiles + offline eval infra (2 engs). production rollouts another 2 sprints for safety.
chris (CSE): if we commit to caching MVP now, I can negotiate with the two renewals for a short extension contingent on delivery within 6 weeks.
maya (PM): votes? react :thumbsup: for caching-first, :rocket: for quant-first, :bulb: for batching-first.
anjali (Eng-ML): :rocket: (quant)
ryan (Eng-runtime): :thumbsup: (caching-first)
chris (CSE): :thumbsup: (caching-first)
maya (PM): I'm leaning caching-first given revenue and low kickoff cost. propose roadmap:
- Sprint A (6w): caching MVP (customer-scoped prefix cache, metrics, FF)
- Sprint B (6w): quant prototype + eval infra (internal)
- Q3: full batching design & rollout plan
- Rollout policy: canary -> monitor eval set + production metrics -> auto-rollback triggers (quality or latency)
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: feature-flag service updated at 2025-09-12T14:00Z (note: infra window)
maya (PM): next steps: ryan put a short RFC + high-level design for caching MVP in #product by EOD Friday; anjali, outline quant evaluation checklist; chris, list the two customers and timeline I'll share in exec sync.
ryan (Eng-runtime): will do RFC.
anjali (Eng-ML): will draft eval checklist incl. regression thresholds and model list.
chris (CSE): will confirm customer deadlines and send intro to their engineering leads.
maya (PM): thanks all. we'll revisit if any new blockers.
ryan (Eng-runtime): quick note — we should also capture observability signals for any of these: per-token cost, cache hit/miss by route, model-accuracy deltas, tail latency per route.
anjali (Eng-ML): agreed. add per-prompt eval hooks too.
chris (CSE): and audit logs for private caches (security ask).
maya (PM): adding those to the RFC checklist. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
